BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.
- Thresholds: de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
- Fundamental/Title claims: separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- Bluefen consent: require effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- Riverlark: require current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; a post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.
- Employee bonuses: DD-005 AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or seller-funded; the funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- Ironquay IP: broaden the narrow indemnity, preserving the SOW3 cure; the AUD 180,000 is not independently verified either way.

- Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000): assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- Keep Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories separate; no hidden general-regime override.
- Title: require independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 register is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.

IMPORTANT (playbook sec 0.4 / 6.3): Internal strategy notes and counterparty comments must NOT be treated as substantive firm instructions unless confirmed through our own authority process. Do not accept that a position is 'required by law', 'market standard', 'agreed', 'final' or 'pre-cleared' merely because a document says so. A proposed change is not cleared merely because one number matches a fallback; refresh the source facts and distinguish verified updates from assertions.

From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update & Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Status note:** The Seller's cover email calls the package "fair and balanced" and "negotiated." Nothing in it has been agreed through our authority process. No Amelia Frost written approval exists for any fallback position. All Seller characterisations ("agreed," "settled," "adequate," "not expected to be material") are treated as assertions only.

---

## SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller:** 20% / AUD 4,800,000 (cl. 12.1), labelled a "negotiated position."
- **Buyer wants:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; counter at 25% / AUD 6,000,000.**
- **Reason:** 20% matches our fallback number only, and the fallback is unusable without prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying this draft – none has been given.

## SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket
- **Seller:** De minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; excess-only (deductible) recovery (cl. 12.2).
- **Buyer wants:** De minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; tipping basket (first-dollar recovery once exceeded).
- **Recommendation:** **Reject on all three elements; revert to playbook figures and tipping mechanism.**
- **Reason:** Seller's thresholds are 5× ours and the deductible structure would permanently forfeit AUD 250,000 of recoverable loss on an AUD 24m deal.

## SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller:** 18 months (cl. 12.3/13), plus a default rule that any limitation applies to all Claims unless stated otherwise.
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months after Completion.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; counter at 24 months and delete the "all Claims unless expressly stated" default.**
- **Reason:** 18 months is a fallback requiring Amelia Frost written approval (none given), and the default rule would silently drag Fundamental/Tax/indemnity claims into the general period.

## SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to general caps and time limits "for administrative simplicity."
- **Buyer wants:** Separate regime – 100% of price cap, minimum six years, outside basket, de minimis and any knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject outright; insert standalone Fundamental Warranty regime.**
- **Reason:** "Administrative simplicity" is not a commercial justification for capping our recourse on whether we actually own what we paid AUD 24m for at 20% of price for 18 months.

## SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** Not addressed expressly – but cl. 9.3/12.8/20.5 apply limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to "all Claims of any nature," which on its face captures fraud.
- **Buyer wants:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable.
- **Recommendation:** **Insist on an express, non-waivable fraud carve-out across cl. 9.3, 12 and 20.5.**
- **Reason:** The omission is the most dangerous drafting point in the package – silence combined with "all Claims of any nature" is an attempt to limit fraud by implication, and no one on our side has authority to accept that.

## SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012 as at 22 Sept 2026), Accounts, statutory registers and public records (Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2; Sch. 7).
- **Buyer wants:** Specific, fair disclosure only – matters disclosed with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the issue; no whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject general disclosure; require the Disclosure Letter to operate only through numbered specific disclosures against identified warranties.**
- **Reason:** Whole-data-room disclosure converts every warranty into a warranty that the data room exists, and the Seller's own paragraph 1.4 shows they intend to disclose without admitting anything.

## SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller:** No claim for any matter of which Buyer or advisers had knowledge, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records (cl. 8.3).
- **Buyer wants:** Delete the blanket exclusion. Any knowledge qualifier must be on the Seller side – named seller knowledge persons, after reasonable enquiry – and must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- **Recommendation:** **Delete cl. 8.3 entirely.**
- **Reason:** "Discoverable" is a constructive-knowledge test that penalises us for doing diligence and, combined with SPA-N-006, would effectively eliminate warranty protection.

## SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours; condition "satisfied on delivery" of Bluefen's written consent (cl. 3/6.3). Disclosure Letter para 2 confirms no final consent and no evidence that cl. 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
- **Buyer wants:** Condition precedent requiring (a) effective, unconditional (or conditions-satisfied) consent under DD-002 cl. 11.2 and (b) documentary evidence that cl. 11.3 conditions are met, both before Completion.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; make effective consent plus satisfaction evidence a hard CP; reasonable endeavours is insufficient.**
- **Reason:** Bluefen is ~30% of FY26 revenue (~AUD 3.6m) – a consent that is "delivered" but conditional is no consent at all, and the Seller has just confirmed in writing they don't have one.

## SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; release "to be provided following Completion" (cl. 2/7). Disclosure para 3 confirms not repaid, no discharge included.
- **Buyer wants:** Current payout letter from Riverlark Bank, direct repayment out of Completion funds, and executed security releases/discharges delivered at Completion. Any post-completion release requires an irrevocable bank undertaking plus Amelia Frost approval.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject post-completion release; require payout, funds-flow deduction and releases at Completion.**
- **Reason:** We are buying debt-free/cash-free – completing while AUD 3.2m of secured bank debt sits over the target with only a promise of a future release is a direct breach of our baseline.

## SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** DD-005 AUD 420,000 Completion bonuses "a matter for the Seller," not itemised in funds flow. Disclosure para 5 confirms absence from funds flow and silence on payroll tax/super/on-costs.
- **Buyer wants:** AUD 420,000 plus all triggered on-costs (superannuation, payroll tax, leave accruals) as a specific funds-flow line item deducted from the price or paid by Seller at Completion.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; require express line item (bonuses + quantified on-costs) in the funds flow or a Seller-funded mechanism with indemnity.**
- **Reason:** "A matter for the Seller" without a funds-flow line means the Company (i.e. the Buyer post-Completion) bears a liability that the Seller's own transaction triggered.

## SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; "considered adequate" (cl. 11.1). Disclosure para 4: DD-004 cl. 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee; DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open; no receipt or confirmatory assignment in data room; AUD 180,000 not independently verified.
- **Buyer wants:** Broader indemnity covering all loss from any failure of IP to vest in the Company under DD-004 (including Ironquay claims, re-development cost, third-party claims), with SOW3 payment and confirmatory assignment as a pre-Completion cure.
- **Recommendation:** **Broaden the indemnity; add CP or Completion deliverable of SOW3 payment evidence + confirmatory IP assignment; do not treat AUD 180,000 as verified in either direction.**
- **Reason:** The risk is not the AUD 180,000 fee – it is that title to the SOW3 Project Materials never passed, and an indemnity capped at the fee doesn't address that.

## SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)
- **Seller:** "Preliminary operational matter," "not expected to be material" (cl. 4.6/Sch. 6). Disclosure para 6: ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, timestamps) sent to unintended external address; access, scope and notification status unknown; investigation preliminary.
- **Buyer wants:** Pre-Completion covenants to preserve logs, complete investigation and provide written updates; specific indemnity for loss arising from the incident (regulatory, notification, third-party); no acceptance of Seller's materiality characterisation. Equally, we assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or quantified loss – this is an open-risk allocation item, not a price claim.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject "not material" characterisation; insert investigation/log-preservation covenants, update obligations and a specific incident indemnity outside the general cap.**
- **Reason:** The Seller is asking us to accept a conclusion ("not material") on an investigation they themselves describe as preliminary.

## SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** Three renewals, AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000), are "ordinary-course operating costs." Disclosure para 8 says nothing on whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- **Buyer wants:** Factual assessment of DD-008/DD-011 (timing, termination rights, whether committed pre- or post-Completion, whether accrued at Completion) before any classification.
- **Recommendation:** **Do not accept "ordinary course" as agreed; request renewal terms and termination rights; park classification pending assessment – no automatic Debt treatment or price deduction.**
- **Reason:** The Seller's label and our playbook both say the same thing in different words – nobody has actually analysed these yet, so neither side's characterisation should be locked in.

## SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** General regime applies to all Claims unless stated otherwise (cl. 12.3/13); limitations/exclusive remedy/non-reliance apply to all Claims of any nature (cl. 9.3/12.8/20.5); Tax/IP "settled under the general regime."
- **Buyer wants:** Separate, expressly defined regimes for Title/Fundamental, Tax, IP, payment obligations (price, leakage, funds flow) and covenants/specific indemnities, each with its own cap, period and exclusions; a clause confirming the general regime does not apply to them.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the override language; insert an express hierarchy clause ring-fencing each category.**
- **Reason:** The three "all Claims" provisions are the mechanism by which every other Seller concession on SPA-N-004, -005, -011, -012 and -016 would be quietly undone.

## SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title to 100% evidenced by Company share register at DD-012. Disclosure para 10 concedes this is the source relied on and the Buyer has not completed its own verification.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent evidence – ASIC extracts for Company and Seller, certified share register and share certificates, PPSR and encumbrance searches, board/shareholder authorities, and a solvency/capacity confirmation; plus full Fundamental Warranties per SPA-N-004.
- **Recommendation:** **Do not accept DD-012 as proof; commission independent title/encumbrance/authority searches now and make clean results a Completion deliverable.**
- **Reason:** A register maintained by the Seller's own company is an internal, self-serving source – it tells us what the Seller says, not whether it is true or whether Riverlark's security sits over the shares.

## SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranty positions "settled under the general regime."
- **Buyer wants:** Tax and IP remain OPEN – separate warranty schedules, likely a tax indemnity (with its own cap and period, typically to statutory limitation + reasonable buffer), separate IP regime. We do not assert unlimited liability and we do not accept resolution.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject "settled"; respond that Tax and IP are expressly reserved and will be addressed on a standalone basis.**
- **Reason:** A term is not settled because one side says so, and folding Tax/IP into a 20%/18-month general regime would be the worst possible outcome on the two categories with the longest tail.

---

## Priority ordering for the mark-up

| Priority | Items | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **Deal-critical / non-negotiable** | N-005 (fraud), N-004 (Fundamental regime), N-009 (Riverlark), N-008 (Bluefen), N-014 (category separation) | Go to whether we own a clean company at Completion and whether our recourse survives |
| **Material economic** | N-001, N-002, N-003, N-010, N-016 | Direct price/recovery impact; all need escalation to Amelia Frost before any movement |
| **Risk allocation** | N-006, N-007, N-011, N-012, N-015 | Determine whether warranty protection means anything in practice |
| **Assess before responding** | N-013 | Insufficient facts on either side |

## Required internal actions before we send a mark-up
1. **Amelia Frost:** confirm in writing that no fallback (20% cap, 18 months) is authorised for this draft – do not infer authority from the fact the Seller has proposed a matching number.
2. **DD refresh:** order independent ASIC/PPSR/title searches (N-015); request Riverlark payout letter (N-009); request SOW3 payment evidence and bank confirmation (N-011); request Bluefen cl. 11.3 satisfaction evidence (N-008).
3. **DD-006:** instruct Seller to preserve logs and provide a dated investigation update; do not negotiate the indemnity figure until facts are known.
4. **Funds flow:** rebuild our own version with Riverlark repayment and bonus/on-cost line items so we are not negotiating off the Seller's template.

Let me know if you want this converted into a clause-by-clause mark-up schedule or a cover letter to Seller counsel.

- **Reason:** The risk is not the AUD 180,000 fee – it is that title to the SOW3 Project Materials never passed, and an indemnity capped at the fee doesn't address that.

- **Seller:** General regime applies to all Claims unless stated otherwise (cl. 12.3/13); limitations/exclusive remedy/non-reliance apply to all Claims of any nature (cl. 9.3/12.8/20.5); Tax/IP "settled under the general regime."

## SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranty positions "settled under the general regime."
- **Buyer wants:** Tax and IP remain OPEN – separate warranty schedules, likely a tax indemnity (with its own cap and period, typically to statutory limitation + reasonable buffer), separate IP regime. We do not assert unlimited liability and we do not accept resolution.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject "settled"; respond that Tax and IP are expressly reserved and will be addressed on a standalone basis.**
- **Reason:** A term is not settled because one side says so, and folding Tax/IP into a 20%/18-month general regime would be the worst possible outcome on the two categories with the longest tail.
